summary: Window animation-step player (named 'queue' by an early pass): both recovered methods drive an embedded animation player at +0xD8C that accumulates a 1/30 s clock and dispatches one of eight 0x18-byte step callbacks through a relocation table. The owning window is not identified, so the class name is only a mechanism description.
evidence: Update 0x003B3EB8 asm: r4 = self + 0xC00 + 0x18C = self+0xD8C; [r4] is the player vtable (slot +0x10 queried, slot +0x14 called by ClearPending 0x003B3E54 with 'is active'); [r4+4]=index < 8, [r4+8] += 1/30f, [r4+0xC]++, [r4+0x10]=delta; entry base r4+0x34+index*0x18, callback resolved through the table at [r4+0x20]. Eight 0x18-byte entries end at +0xE80, so the 3504-byte struct_db size is a lower bound only; no caller names the owner.

fields.name: animPlayerVtable
fields.evidence: player object starts at +0xD8C and its first word is the vtable: ClearPending loads piVar2 = self+0xD8C and calls (**(code**)(*piVar2 + 0x14))(piVar2,0) then slot +0x10 to stop it; Update calls slot +0x10 with r0 = self+0xD8C

fields.name: animPlayerSlotIndex
fields.evidence: asm ldr r0,[r4,#4]; cmp r0,#8 with r4=self+0xD8C; entry address = r4 + index*0x18 + 0x34

fields.name: animPlayerElapsed
fields.evidence: asm vldr s0,[r4,#8]; vadd.f32 s0,s0,s16 (s16 = 1/30f); vstr s0,[r4,#8] when the player reports inactive

fields.name: animPlayerTick
fields.evidence: asm ldr r1,[r4,#0xC]; add r1,r1,#1; str r1,[r4,#0xC] on every update; integer counter, not a float despite the batch type hint

fields.evidence: asm vstr s16,[r4,#0x10] with s16 = 1/30f each update (last frame delta)

summary: Base class of the UI fade/curve animator: 13 channels of {float value, flags} starting at +4 are stepped toward 1.0, 0.5 and 0.0, and three words record which channels reached each threshold. Ui_FadeAnimator derives from it and replaces the vtable.
evidence: Ctor 0x005F9CCC stores vtable 0x0077F70C, clears +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74, stores 0.5f (0x3F000000) at +0x78 and 0.1f (0x3DCCCCCD) at +0x7C, then zeroes 0x68 bytes at +4 (=13 eight-byte channels). The step loop after 0x005F9768 reads vldr s2,[entry+4], compares with 1.0f, subtracts [self+0x78], compares with [self+0x7C], and ORs the caller's channel mask into [self+0x6C] / [self+0x70]. Ui_FadeAnimator_InitCurveA/B (0x005F8F20/0x005F9740) call this ctor and overwrite the vtable.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: base ctor stores 0x0077F70C; Ui_FadeAnimator_InitCurveA/B overwrite it with 0x0077F6B4 / 0x0077F6FC

fields.evidence: step-loop asm ORs the channel mask into [self+0x6C] when a channel's float value equals 1.0f

fields.name: maybe_reachedMidMask
fields.evidence: step-loop asm ORs the mask into [self+0x70] after snapping a channel to the 0.5f target stored at +0x78

fields.name: maybe_reachedMinMask
fields.evidence: third accumulated mask word; the step loop reads [self+0x74] and ORs the channel mask in the 0.0 branch

fields.name: maybe_midTarget
fields.evidence: ctor stores 0.5f (0x3F000000); the step loop subtracts it from the channel value before comparing with +0x7C

fields.name: maybe_snapTolerance
fields.evidence: ctor stores 0.1f (0x3DCCCCCD); the step loop compares (value - 0.5f) with it to decide whether to snap the channel to 0.5f
